subject.title: [Bug]: Enabling Codex plugin causes Runtime to switch to OpenAI Codex and ignore configured primary model, resulting in GPT-5.4-nano TPM failures

question: For an existing session that has an explicit `/model openai/...` selection and a configured DeepSeek primary, should enabling the Codex plugin keep the explicit OpenAI selection and let it use the default Codex runtime, or should plugin enablement/hot reload reset ordinary chat to the configured primary unless Codex was explicitly requested after enablement?
rationale: Current docs and tests preserve explicit session model choices and make official OpenAI routes use Codex by default, but the issue asks for a different operator expectation that could change runtime/session compatibility semantics.

options.title: Preserve explicit selections
options.body: Keep `/model openai/...` as the active session model across plugin reloads, and fix only unintended model promotion plus status/doctor clarity gaps.

options.title: Reset on Codex enablement
options.body: Treat Codex plugin enablement as a reason to return ordinary sessions to configured primary unless the user selects Codex/OpenAI afterward, accepting a session-state compatibility change.

options.title: Fold into resolver refactor
options.body: Defer this issue to the broader selected/runtime/auth-state resolver work and avoid a narrow fix until that design lands.

recommendation.title: Preserve explicit selections
recommendation.body: Keep `/model openai/...` as the active session model across plugin reloads, and fix only unintended model promotion plus status/doctor clarity gaps.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent OpenAI provider unification, harness policy, and Codex/session runtime history make this the strongest available routing owner for the product-semantics choice.
